title: Representative independence of the summand trace
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the joint conventions of [def-trf-karoubi-trace], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and the fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$ and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix one compactification of $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ over $k_0$ for the compact-support functor and the chosen Frobenius exchange of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], and use its base change at every coefficient stage. Use the common-stage coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $(E,K)$ and $(F,L)$, with $E,F\subset\Qlb$ finite over $\Ql$, represent an object $A\in D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ through specified isomorphisms $\alpha:(E,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and $\beta:(F,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$. Put $h=\beta^{-1}\alpha$.

There is a finite intermediate extension $M\supset E,F$ and an isomorphism $w:K\otimes_E M\xrightarrow{\sim}L\otimes_F M$ representing $h$. Any finite family of endomorphisms, idempotents and compatibility equations involving $h$ can be represented simultaneously after enlarging $M$. Compatible endomorphisms mean ones satisfying $hv_K=v_Lh$ in the common-stage category; for summands the isomorphism and this equation are on the corresponding summands. For the transported perfect coefficient complexes and summands of [def-trf-karoubi-trace], their traces agree after applying $E\hookrightarrow M$ and $F\hookrightarrow M$, hence in $\Qlb$. The comparison is independent of further enlargement, of the morphism representatives, and of the choice of a splitting of a summand.

For the Frobenius assertion, require that the representatives are of the same Weil datum: they carry Weil structures $\varphi_K:Lg_\gamma^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ and $\varphi_L:Lg_\gamma^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. After transporting these maps and $h$ to the common stage $M$ (using the scalar-extension and pullback comparisons), require the well-typed intertwining equation $w\varphi_{K,M}=\varphi_{L,M}Lg_{\gamma,M}^*(w)$. Here the global operator is $F_{c,K}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi_K)\tau_{c,K}$ of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], where $\tau_c$ is the transport of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. For $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with its specified geometric point $\bar y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$, the local operator is $F_{y,m,K}=(\varphi_K^{[m]})_{\bar y}\tau_{y,m,K}$. The iterated Weil map is $\varphi_K^{[m]}=\varphi_KG(\varphi_K)\cdots G^{m-1}(\varphi_K)$ for $G=Lg_\gamma^*$. The stalk transport $\tau_{y,m,K}$ is the $m$-fold point transport of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] on $\bar y^*K$, followed by the pullback identification from $g_\gamma^m\bar y=\bar y g_s^m$; pullbacks and stalk evaluation use [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Thus its target is $(G^mK)_{\bar y}$. These are geometric Frobenius transports, with $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ as in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Then the global operators and their powers, and the local operators for every $m\geq1$, have the same traces on corresponding invariant summands in $\Qlb$. For a third representative with representing map $\delta$, the comparison $\delta^{-1}\alpha$ is the composite $(\delta^{-1}\beta)(\beta^{-1}\alpha)$, so these comparisons are transitive relative to the specified representing maps.

Consequently, whenever the lattice and finite-level hypotheses of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] hold for a finite representative, its trace identity, transported to $\Qlb$, depends only on this represented Weil datum and not on its finite coefficient field, representative or summand splitting. This is independence of the transported trace values; it does not assert that arbitrary Weil structures on the same underlying coefficient object are compatible.

proof.text: Use the framework category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with its rational stages and scalar extension of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; this is not an identification with the distinct PBC coefficient categories. Represent $h$ and $h^{-1}$ over finite fields. The displayed Hom-colimit definition says that each equality of morphism classes is witnessed at a further finite field. Choose fields witnessing $h^{-1}h=1$, $hh^{-1}=1$ and the finitely many specified compatibility equations; a compositum of this finite list contains them all. Transport the representatives there, using the natural composition comparisons of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. The definition of composition in the common-stage category now gives $zu=1$ and $uz=1$ over that stage, hence $w=u$ is an isomorphism with inverse $z$. Include every specified endomorphism, idempotent and compatibility equation in the finite list. Equality witnesses persist on enlargement by functoriality. This is the finite-diagram argument directly from the framework Hom definition; it invokes no theorem for a different integral category.

source.place: sentence 1: common-stage representative and its inverse, with all finite compatibility equations

proof.text: Work over a finite coefficient field, and at each common finite overfield, with the perfect coefficient complexes of [def-trf-karoubi-trace]. Apply [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] to replace each complex and its derived endomorphisms by graded cohomology. Its image/kernel splitting of an idempotent $e$ makes $ve$ block diagonal with blocks $v_S$ and zero. Thus the FIELD supertrace clause of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] gives $\operatorname{tr}(ve\mid P)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(H^i(v_S))=\operatorname{tr}(v_S\mid S)$, exactly the summand trace of [def-trf-karoubi-trace]. For corresponding summands with intertwining isomorphism $w$, choose a basis on each $H^i(S)$ and its image under $H^i(w)$ on the other summand; the matrices have equal entries, hence equal diagonal sums and signed traces. For two splittings of a single idempotent the cited splitting lemma supplies the isomorphism $r'i$ with inverse $ri'$ intertwining the restrictions. This proves independence of the chosen splitting and compares summands in distinct ambient perfect complexes without comparing their complements.

source.place: First sentence: summand trace after common-stage isomorphism; returned Step 2 with field splitting extracted.

proof.text: For $E\subset M$, use the field-supertrace clause of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws]. The natural comparison of [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension] identifies $H^i(P\otimes_E M)$ with $H^i(P)\otimes_E M$ and intertwines the cohomology endomorphisms; it also preserves the bounded finite-dimensional range. The cited comparison is natural on complexes and takes quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Therefore it is natural on a derived morphism represented by a roof: apply naturality to both arrows and invert the quasi-isomorphism arrow. This justifies its use for the derived endomorphism $ve$. In an $E$-basis the matrix of $H^i(ve)$ after extension has the same entries mapped into $M$; its trace is the image of the sum of the diagonal entries. Summing with the same signs proves $\iota_{M/E}(\operatorname{tr}_E(ve\mid P))=\operatorname{tr}_M(v_Me_M\mid P_M)$. This explicitly proves the required field-extension trace law, without treating the finite-ring variable $A=A_{E,n}$ in the other clauses as a field. Step 2 equates the compatible summand traces at the common stage. If representatives or fields differ, the eventual-equality rule of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] compares their finite list of maps and equations at a further compositum $N$, exactly as in Step 1. The calculations agree there, hence in $\Qlb$; injectivity of a field inclusion also equates calculations already in the same smaller field.

source.place: sentences 1-2: scalar-extension law and independence of the chosen common stage

proof.text: Apply the framework compact-support and stalk functors to $w$. For $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ use [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The common-stage scalar-extension comparisons for compact supports in [lem-fix-operation-reduction], followed by [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], give $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes_E M\cong R\Gamma_c(X,K\otimes_E M)$. For a stalk at $\bar y:s\to X$, use the pullback comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], rationalized on integral representatives, and then the sections comparison, giving $K_{\bar y}\otimes_E M\cong(K\otimes_E M)_{\bar y}$. Apply the $F$ versions and the functor on $w$ to compare both realizations; their inverses use $w^{-1}$. These comparisons are natural and compatible with successive extensions by their cited statements. Here $\ell\ne p$, $X$ and $s$ are finite-type over $k$, and $a_X$ is separated of finite type, so [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] gives the bounded constructible integral output needed before rationalization. Pullback to $\bar y$ preserves bounded constructibility by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], rationalized as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The point functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] takes these outputs into bounded finite-dimensional complexes. By [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] (the splitting lemma of Step 2) this bounded finite-dimensional complex is perfect. Steps 2-3 apply to these realizations and their summands.

source.place: sentence 1: the transported perfect coefficient complexes for compact support and stalks

proof.text:
For Frobenius include the one-step equation $h\varphi_K=\varphi_L Lg_\gamma^*(h)$ in the finite diagram of Step 1. This is the Weil-morphism condition of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and is an additional condition, not a consequence of an isomorphism of underlying objects. The pullback comparisons in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], rationalized on integral representatives, let us read it at $M$ as $w\varphi_{K,M}=\varphi_{L,M}G(w)$ with $G=Lg_{\gamma,M}^*$. If $w\varphi_K^{[m]}=\varphi_L^{[m]}G^m(w)$, multiply the pullback of this identity by the one-step identity to obtain
$$w\varphi_KG(\varphi_K^{[m]})=\varphi_LG(w\varphi_K^{[m]})=\varphi_LG(\varphi_L^{[m]})G^{m+1}(w).$$
Together with the base case $m=1$, this proves the intertwining identity for every $m\ge1$, with the canonical pullback composition identifications understood. Here $\varphi^{[m]}$ is defined by the displayed product of $m$ pullbacks of the Weil map; it is defined for every object of the rationalized category, without a finite-Tor hypothesis on its reductions. The induction uses only functoriality and the stated one-step relation. One common stage works for all iterates; no assertion about descending an infinite diagram is needed.

source.place: last sentence: Frobenius compatibility and all its iterates; explicit induction

proof.text:
At the common stage put $C=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ and $G=Lg_\gamma^*$. Naturality of $t_K=\tau_{c,K}$ in [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] says $C(Gw)t_K=t_LC(w)$. With the global operator of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] and Step 5, this gives
$$C(w)F_{c,K}=C(\varphi_L)C(Gw)t_K=F_{c,L}C(w).$$
Multiplication and induction give $C(w)F_{c,K}^m=F_{c,L}^mC(w)$ for every $m\geq1$. These equations restrict to the corresponding invariant summands.

source.place: Last sentence: global intertwining, first paragraph of returned Step 6.

proof.text:
For $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, use $J_y$ and $t_{y,m}$ of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization]. Its naturality equation is $J_y(G^mw)t_{y,m,K}=t_{y,m,L}J_y(w)$. Apply $J_y$ to the iterated Weil equation of Step 5 and compose with $t_{y,m,K}$ to obtain
$$J_y(w)J_y(\varphi_K^{[m]})t_{y,m,K}=J_y(\varphi_L^{[m]})t_{y,m,L}J_y(w),$$
which is $J_y(w)F_{y,m,K}=F_{y,m,L}J_y(w)$. The same cited lemma identifies this point transport with the specified $\kappa^{(m)}$-normalized transport on the strict reduction diagrams, then on their integral realization and rationalization. This use is on arbitrary framework constructible objects; no finite-Tor hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Last sentence: local intertwining and geometric normalization; middle paragraphs of returned Step 6.

proof.text: The comparison of compact-support transports before and after coefficient extension is the displayed equation of [lem-trf-frobenius-transports-scalar-extension]; the corresponding stalk equation is the last displayed equation of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization]. Naturality of the realization comparisons in Step 4, applied to $\varphi$, supplies the remaining factor of each Frobenius operator. Thus these comparisons intertwine the operators before extension with those used in Steps 6 and 7. Composition gives the same assertion for global powers. Restrict to corresponding invariant summands and apply Steps 2 and 3 to equate their traces. The normalization and coefficient claims are about the specified maps constructed on simultaneous models, rather than a uniqueness assertion from their reductions.

source.place: Last sentence: coefficient compatibility, last paragraph of returned Step 6.

proof.text: For specified representing maps $\alpha,\beta,\delta$, cancellation gives $(\delta^{-1}\beta)(\beta^{-1}\alpha)=\delta^{-1}\alpha$. The eventual-equality rule of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with the finite compositum construction of Step 1, realizes this equality at one finite stage. Applying the functors in Step 4 preserves composition. The scalar-composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], the compatibility with successive extensions in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], the common-stage operation comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], and the explicit composition equation of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identify the successive realization comparisons with the direct one. Step 3 removes the extra field. This proves transitivity relative to the specified representing maps and equality of traces.

Apply [lem-trf-global-frobenius-iterate-formula] with $G=Lg_\gamma^*$, $C=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$, $t=\tau_c$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] and the Weil map $\varphi$. This yields $F_c^m=C(\varphi^{[m]})t_K^{[m]}$ for the operator of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. The explicit composite defining $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ in [def-trf-frobenius-operators] is $t_K^{[m]}$ followed by the inverse pullback-composition identification. The corresponding identification in the iterated Weil map cancels it. Hence these powers are exactly the iterated global operators of the trace-formula convention, at the finite stages where that definition applies and after its specified integral realization and rationalization.

source.place: Trace-formula consequence: identification of global powers, induction extracted from returned Step 8.

proof.text: When the hypotheses of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] hold for a representative, apply that theorem there using the fixed compactification. Its finite-level hypotheses invoke [thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula], whose domain includes $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$. Thus [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] applies at this stage. It identifies the one-step global operator with [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], and its stalk normalization agrees with Step 7. Step 10 identifies all global powers. This use of the rational-model theorem is restricted to the representative satisfying the finite-level hypotheses; Steps 1–9 required no finite-Tor assumption. The bounded finite-dimensional cohomology conclusion of the trace-formula theorem and the FIELD supertrace clause of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] identify its terms with the categorical global trace and the categorical stalk traces. Map the equality to $\Qlb$. Steps 3–8 identify each trace with the value from every compatible finite representative of the same Weil datum, including a corresponding summand presentation. The rational-point indexing set depends only on $X_0$ and $m$, so it is unchanged and its terms agree. Step 9 supplies coherence for three representatives. This proves independence of the transported identity, retaining the finite-level etale-origin and exceptional-adjoint hypotheses; none follows merely from an underlying-object isomorphism.

source.place: Final consequence: conditional E-stage formula; remainder of returned Step 8.

It constructs global and local operators directly from cohomology/point transports on the full constructible domain, and checks the scheme-Frobenius normalization on finite reduction diagrams; no finite-Tor lattice hypothesis is taken from the rational-model theorem. Uses the existing field-cohomology scalar comparison, explicit vector-space contractions, preservation lemmas, and coefficient/exchange naturality. Retains the full hypotheses in the final E-stage trace-formula consequence. No new nodes or exact Lean/Mathlib attachment. Second reading fixes the common compactification, spells out the homotopy-localization and rational fixed-point calculations, and explicitly identifies the conditional trace-formula operators using the rational-model theorem only on its finite-Tor domain. Return repair: revalidated every proof citation against the current DAG, made the field-supertrace domain explicit in Step 2, and refreshed the three trace-law quotations to the complete current field clause; no triangle-additivity assertion is used. Independent second reading: made both splitting inverse products, the restriction intertwining, and derived-roof naturality explicit; cited the existing integral pullback composition, Frobenius trivialization pullback naturality, and scheme/Galois coefficient-change statements for Step 6. NQ re-split repair: retained the returned statement and Lean record, and original Steps 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7 verbatim. Extracted field-complex splitting, local Frobenius normalization, coefficient compatibility of the chosen compact-support transport, and the general transport-power identity into four self-contained statement-only nodes. Replaced returned Steps 2, 6 and 8 by short applications and the remaining explicit matrix/intertwining calculations. Corrected provisional extraction metadata and search attribution; reused the existing cohomology comparison instead of a duplicate scalar-trace node.
